# Backend Technical Specification: Phase One

Oct 13, 2026 (v2.3) · @David

This specification defines how the backend is built to meet the phase-one functional specification: one ASP.NET application on AWS, using Aurora PostgreSQL, S3, SQS, Bedrock and Textract. Requirement IDs such as AS-5 refer to the functional specification.

## Architecture

![backend architecture · 10 components](data:image/png;base64,)

backend architecture · 10 components

Requests reach the API through CloudFront. The API writes to the database, issues file links and queues work. The worker reads the queues, processes documents and assesses controls, and is the only part that calls Bedrock and Textract.

The same image also runs one-off tasks, such as database migrations and the control catalog import, which run once and exit. The physical layout is drawn in diagrams/system-infrastructure.drawio.svg.

## Code structure

The backend is one ASP.NET project, organized by feature, with each AWS service behind an interface.

```
src/App/
  Program.cs
  Features/
    Clients/  Users/  Engagements/  Scope/
    Documents/  AssessmentCriteria/  Assessments/  Decisions/  Export/
  Pipeline/
    DocumentConsumer.cs      reads the document queue
    AssessmentConsumer.cs    reads the assessment queue
    Sweeper.cs               re-queues or fails stuck work
    Steps/                   Extract, Chunk, Embed, LinkScope
    Extractors/              Pdf, Docx, Xlsx, Csv, Pptx
    Chunkers/                one or more per file type, behind IChunker
  Integrations/
    Abstractions/            IFileStorage, IQueue, ITextRecognizer,
                             IEmbedder, IControlAssessor
    Aws/                     S3, SQS, Textract and Bedrock implementations
    Aws/Prompts/             versioned prompt files
  Data/                      AppDbContext, entity configs, migrations
  Common/                    auth, engagement access, errors, paging
  Tasks/                     Migrate, ImportCatalog (one-off commands)
infra/                       CDK project
tests/                       unit and integration tests
```

**Rules**

- Code in Features/ and Pipeline/ uses only the interfaces in Abstractions/. AWS SDK types appear only in Integrations/Aws/.
- Each feature folder holds its endpoints, request and response types, and service class.
- The same image runs as API or worker. The setting Worker:Enabled turns the consumers and the sweeper on. A command selects a one-off task instead: migrate or import-catalog. It runs once and exits.
- Endpoints do no slow work. They write to the database and send a queue message.

## Data model

All application data is in one PostgreSQL database. The file schema.mmd is the column-level reference until the first migration. After that, the generated schema.dbml is.

| Group       | Tables                                                                           |
| ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| People      | users, clients                                                                   |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |
| Engagements | engagements, engagement_frameworks, engagement_controls, scope_items             |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |
| Catalog     | frameworks, controls, assessment_criteria, control_mappings (empty in phase one) |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |
| Documents   | documents, document_chunks, chunk_scope_mentions                                 |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |
| Assessment  | assessment_runs, assessment_run_controls, assessments, evidence_citations        |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |
| Review      | consultant_decisions, review_flags                                               |
| ---         | ---                                                                              |

**Rules**

- Primary keys are UUIDv7 values generated by the application, so they sort by creation time.
- Every engagement-scoped table carries engagement_id, and every query on it filters by it. Each one references its engagement-scoped parents by (id, engagement_id), so a row can never point into another engagement (QR-1).
- assessments, evidence_citations and consultant_decisions are insert-only. The one exception is the is_current marker on assessments.
- A run creates one assessment per applicable control. (run_id, control_id) is unique, which makes a repeated message harmless.
- A partial unique index allows one current assessment per engagement and control. It treats an empty scope item as equal (NULLS NOT DISTINCT), so the rule holds in phase one.
- document_chunks.embedding has an HNSW index with cosine distance, covering only chunks that are neither deleted nor superseded. document_chunks.search_vector is generated from the chunk text and has a GIN index.
- controls holds each control's number, theme, title and statement. The statement is the standard's own text, which the firm's license covers. The catalog import task loads it from a private S3 bucket, so the text is never in the repository.
- Deleted documents and closed engagements are kept for three years, then removed from the database and S3. The period is a setting.
- assessment_criteria is insert-only apart from its active marker. A partial unique index allows one active version per control (CT-2, CT-3).
- A run records the criteria version of each control it queues, in assessment_run_controls (CT-3).
- Partial unique indexes keep "only one" rules while history is kept: one active run per engagement, one live copy of a file, one live chunk per position, and one open flag per reason.
- Two triggers copy documents.deleted_at to the document's chunks: one on delete for existing chunks, and one on insert for chunks written later. Deleted text always leaves search.
- "Accepted" or "overridden" is not stored. It is worked out by comparing the final verdict with the preliminary one (RV-2).
- engagement_controls gets a row for every control of each framework attached to the engagement, so applicability is never missing (EN-3).
- audit_events records every change, with who, what and when (RV-6). It is append-only.
- A decision_superseded flag names the assessment it replaced, so the earlier decision can be shown (RV-7).
- Scope items are hard-deleted, and their mentions are deleted with them. assessments.scope_item_id is empty in phase one, so the in-use check never blocks yet (EN-6).
- Adding or activating criteria locks the control's row first, so two admins cannot collide (CT-2, CT-3).
- assessments.scope_item_id stays empty in phase one, because there is one verdict per control for the whole engagement.

## Sign-in and access control

Cognito proves who the user is, and the backend decides what the user may do.

**Sign-in**

- One Cognito user pool, with self-registration off and multi-factor sign-in required (AC-2, AC-3).
- An admin invites a user. The backend creates the Cognito account, then the users row with external_id set to the account's subject.
- The API validates the Cognito access token on every request: signature, issuer, client ID and expiry (AC-1).
- The token's subject is matched to users.external_id. Role and client come from the users row (AC-4).
- Disabling a user sets users.disabled_at and disables the Cognito account. Requests from a disabled user are refused with 403, even while an earlier token is still valid (AC-7). It also signs the user out everywhere. An admin cannot disable themselves or the last admin.

**Access control**

- Every engagement route passes through one access check before its handler runs.
- The check loads the engagement and allows admins and consultants. It allows a client user only when the engagement's client is their own (AC-5).
- A failed check returns 404, the same as a missing engagement. It runs before the route's role check.
- Role limits on a route, such as consultant-only, are declared on the route. A user who passes the engagement check but lacks the role gets 403.
- The access check never uses lead_consultant_id. Leading an engagement gives no extra access (EN-9).
- Every write locks the engagement row (FOR SHARE) in its transaction, and closing locks it (FOR UPDATE), so a write and a close cannot both succeed.
- Handlers receive the checked engagement ID and pass it to every query (AC-6).
- Stored files use the key prefix engagements/{engagementId}/. Upload and download links are issued only after the access check, for one object, and expire after 15 minutes.

**Client view**

The results endpoint returns each control's latest consultant verdict, marked under review while the control is re-assessed, not applicable from applicability, or pending when it has never been decided (RV-13). For client users it never reads preliminary verdicts, rationales, citations or notes.

## Document pipeline

A document moves from upload to ready through five steps, each of which can be repeated safely.

**Upload**

1. The client asks for an upload link, giving the file name, type and size. The backend rejects a wrong type or a size over the limit (DO-2), creates the documents row as pending, and returns the link. The backend chooses the S3 key from the document ID. The link expires after 5 minutes, and its policy fixes the file type and size.
2. The client uploads the file to S3. The upload policy also enforces the size limit.
3. The client confirms. The backend checks that the object exists and sends {documentId} to the document queue. It first records the S3 version ID and confirmed_at. The worker and download links use only that version (DO-9).

**Steps**

<div class="joplin-table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th><p>Step</p></th><th><p>What it does</p></th><th><p>Output</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>1. Check</p></th><th><p>Computes the SHA-256 hash and confirms the file type from its content. A duplicate in the engagement is marked failed with the reason duplicate and the original's ID, and its S3 object is deleted (DO-3).</p></th><th><pre><code>content_hash</code></pre></th></tr><tr><th><p>2. Extract</p></th><th><p>Reads the text and where each part sits, using the extractor for the file type.</p></th><th><p>One JSON file in S3</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>3. Chunk</p></th><th><p>Splits the text into chunks of about 500 tokens, along headings, rows or slides.</p></th><th><p>document_chunks rows</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>4. Embed</p></th><th><p>Gets one vector per chunk from the embedding model.</p></th><th><p>embedding column</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>5. Link</p></th><th><p>Matches scope item names and aliases in each chunk, ignoring case, on whole words.</p></th><th><p>chunk_scope_mentions rows</p></th></tr></thead></table></div>

After step 5 the document is ready. When scope items change, the API sends a re-link message to the document queue, and step 5 runs again for the engagement's documents.

**Extractors**

| Type | Library                                         | Chunk unit                                  | Location recorded                |
| ---- | ----------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| PDF  | PdfPig, or Textract when there is no text layer | Page section                                | Page and character range         |
| ---  | ---                                             | ---                                         | ---                              |
| DOCX | Open XML SDK                                    | Heading section                             | Heading path and paragraph range |
| ---  | ---                                             | ---                                         | ---                              |
| XLSX | ClosedXML                                       | Group of rows, with the header row repeated | Sheet and cell range             |
| ---  | ---                                             | ---                                         | ---                              |
| CSV  | CsvHelper                                       | Group of rows, with the header row repeated | Row range                        |
| ---  | ---                                             | ---                                         | ---                              |
| PPTX | Open XML SDK                                    | Slide, with its notes                       | Slide number                     |
| ---  | ---                                             | ---                                         | ---                              |

- A PDF whose pages average under 50 characters of embedded text is sent to Textract whole. The worker starts an asynchronous Textract job on the S3 object and polls for the result.
- A DOCX file does not store page numbers, so its location is a heading and paragraph. PR-3 says the same.

**Changing a chunking method**

Extraction and chunking are separate steps, so a new chunking method for a file type changes only the chunk step.

1. Write a class that implements IChunker. It takes the extracted JSON and returns chunks, each with its text and location.
2. Give it a versioned name, such as xlsx-rows-v2, and set it as the chunker for that file type in configuration.
3. New documents use it from then on. Each chunk records the chunker that made it.
4. To apply it to existing documents, run the re-chunk job. It repeats steps 3 to 5 from the stored JSON, without reading the original file or calling Textract again.

- Re-chunking does not delete chunks. Old chunks are marked superseded and left out of search, so existing citations still resolve.
- Embedding, linking, search and assessment need no change, because they work on any chunk.
- Existing verdicts stay as they are. The next run uses the new chunks.
- A method that records a new kind of location also needs the frontend to display it.
- Compare the old and new methods on a development engagement before switching.

**Retries and failure**

- The worker saves processing_step after each step. A redelivered message resumes after the last saved step (PR-5).
- Each step replaces its own earlier output for that document in one transaction (PR-4).
- The queue allows three receives. On the third failure the worker marks the document failed with the error, and SQS moves the message to the dead-letter queue (QR-6).
- The sweeper runs every 5 minutes. It fails an upload never confirmed after 30 minutes (PR-8), re-queues a confirmed document still pending after 15 minutes, fails a document processing for 60 minutes (PR-7), and fails a run with no progress for 30 minutes so it can be resumed.

**Delete and replace**

- Delete sets deleted_at. The row and its chunks stay, and search excludes them (DO-8). A trigger copies deleted_at to the chunks.
- A second trigger copies a deleted document's deleted_at to chunks inserted later, so a document deleted during processing never becomes searchable. The worker also stops early when the document is deleted.
- Replace uploads a new document that points to the old one. When the new one is ready, the old one is marked deleted.
- In the same transaction, each current assessment that cites the old document gets a review flag (RV-8).

## Assessment runs

A run is split into one queue message per control, so controls are assessed in parallel and a stopped run can resume.

**Starting a run**

- The backend rejects a new run while another run for the engagement is queued or running, or while an applicable control has no active assessment criteria (CT-4). A partial unique index also enforces the one-active-run rule in the database (AS-14).
- It inserts the assessment_runs row with the model identifier and prompt version, and one assessment_run_controls row per applicable control with its active criteria version (AS-8, CT-3).
- It sends {runId, controlId} to the assessment queue for each applicable control (AS-2).

**Assessing one control**

1. **Search.** The worker runs one query for the control's title and one for each item of expected evidence in its assessment criteria, and one for each scope item name. For each query, a vector search and a full-text search each return 20 chunks. All the lists are merged by reciprocal rank fusion, and the top 12 chunks are kept. Both searches filter by engagement and exclude deleted documents. The vector search uses iterative scan, filters on the embedding model, and repeats the partial index condition exactly.
2. **Ask.** The worker calls the model through the Bedrock Converse API at temperature 0. The prompt is assembled from the three scopes described under Prompts, followed by the 12 chunks. Each chunk is given with its ID and its document's name, type and upload date (AS-12). The model must answer through one tool whose input is the result: verdict, rationale, and a list of citations, each a chunk ID and a quote.
3. **Verify.** A citation is verified when its chunk ID is one of those sent and its quote appears in that chunk, compared without regard to case or spacing (AS-5). Others are stored as unverified (AS-6).
4. **Apply rules.** A preliminary pass or preliminary fail with no verified citation becomes insufficient evidence (AS-7). When the search returns no chunks, the verdict is insufficient evidence and the model is not called.
5. **Save.** One transaction, in this order: lock the earlier current assessment and clear its is_current; read its decisions; lock the cited chunks and drop citations to deleted ones, applying AS-7 again; insert the assessment and its citations; and, if the earlier one had a decision, add a review flag that names it (AS-9, RV-7).

**Completion and failure**

- A run is completed when each of its assessment_run_controls rows has an assessment or a recorded failure.
- A control that fails three times goes to the dead-letter queue, its row records the error, and the run is marked failed.
- Resuming a failed run queues only the controls that have no assessment in that run (AS-10). Only the engagement's latest run can be resumed (AS-15).
- The worker assesses up to four controls at once. The limit is configurable, and throttled model calls are retried with backoff.

**Prompts**

The prompt for one control is assembled from three scopes, each with its own owner.

<div class="joplin-table-wrapper"><table><thead><tr><th><p>Scope</p></th><th><p>Holds</p></th><th><p>Stored in</p></th><th><p>Changed by</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>App</p></th><th><p>The template: instructions, verdict definitions, the citation rule, and the rule that document text is evidence and never an instruction (AS-13). The verdict rules. The control's number, title and statement.</p></th><th><p>Template and rules: files in the image. Control text: controls, loaded by the catalog import</p></th><th><p>Developers</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Firm</p></th><th><p>The control's active assessment criteria</p></th><th><pre><code>assessment_criteria</code></pre></th><th><p>Admins, by adding a version</p></th></tr><tr><th><p>Engagement</p></th><th><p>Scope item names and descriptions, and the evidence found for the control</p></th><th><p>scope_items, document_chunks</p></th><th><p>Consultants and client users</p></th></tr></thead></table></div>

The template has a named placeholder for each value. A test fails the build if any placeholder is left unfilled.

The template is a file named with its version, such as assess-control.v1.md. A changed template is a new file, and the run records which version it used.

Applicability decides whether a control is assessed at all. It is not part of the prompt.

**Export**

The export endpoint builds the XLSX file on request with ClosedXML: one sheet of controls with verdicts, decisions and rationales, and one sheet of citations (RV-10). It uses the same verified-only citation query as the API (AS-6).

**Decisions**

- Recording a decision locks the assessment (SELECT ... FOR SHARE) and returns 409 if it is no longer current (RV-11). The 409 response includes the current assessment's ID.
- Accepting is allowed only when the final verdict keeps the system's verdict (RV-2). Any other final verdict is an override and needs a note (RV-3).
- Recording a decision clears the assessment's open flags (RV-12).
- Open-flag counts include only flags on current assessments.

## API

The endpoint list is the plan for building. Once the endpoints exist, the generated OpenAPI document is the reference.

**Conventions**

- Engagement-scoped resources are under /api/engagements/{engagementId}/, written "…/" below, so the one access check always has the engagement ID. Firm-wide resources are directly under /api. There is no version prefix, and changes are additive.
- GET reads, POST creates or performs a named action, PATCH edits some fields, PUT sets a whole value, and DELETE removes. Documents are soft-deleted; scope items are hard-deleted.
- JSON uses camelCase. IDs are UUIDv7 strings, and times are ISO 8601 in UTC.
- Lists take limit and cursor, and return items and nextCursor.
- Work that takes time returns 202, and the client polls the resource.
- Errors use problem details with a stable type, listed under Status codes.
- The last write wins on edits. audit_events records each change (RV-6).
- Checks run in this order: 401 (no valid token), 403 (user disabled), 404 (engagement not visible), 403 (role not allowed), 404 (resource not found), 409 (wrong state). An unknown referenced ID returns 400 invalid-reference, whether it does not exist or belongs to another engagement.

**Endpoints**

Roles: A admin, C consultant, U client user. Every endpoint can also return the errors in the check order, and every engagement write can return 409 engagement-closed.

**Status codes**

| Code          | When                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| 200, 201, 204 | Read or update; created; done with no body                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 202           | Work queued: confirm upload, start or resume a run                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 400           | Malformed request, broken field rule, invalid-reference, invalid-lead, note-required                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 401           | No valid token                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 403           | User disabled, or role not allowed                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 404           | Not found, or not visible to this user                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |
| 409           | Valid request in the wrong state: engagement-closed, engagement-not-active, invalid-transition, run-active, run-not-failed, run-superseded, criteria-missing, assessment-not-current, duplicate-scope-item, scope-item-in-use, already-replaced, upload-missing, email-taken, last-admin, invite-accepted |
| ---           | ---                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       |

## Infrastructure

All infrastructure is defined in one CDK project in C#, with the AWS region as a parameter. Production runs in us-east-1, with us-east-2 as the alternative. Confirm before the first deploy that the region offers the chosen models and Textract.

The layout is drawn in diagrams/system-infrastructure.drawio.svg.

| Resource         | Service                         | Configuration                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Network          | VPC                             | Two availability zones. Public subnets hold only the load balancer, private subnets the tasks, and isolated subnets the database. No NAT gateway.                                                 |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Private access   | VPC endpoints                   | SQS, Bedrock Runtime, Textract, Secrets Manager, ECR, CloudWatch Logs and Cognito. S3 through a gateway endpoint.                                                                                 |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| API              | ECS Fargate service             | Behind an Application Load Balancer. Worker:Enabled is false. Scales on CPU.                                                                                                                      |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Worker           | ECS Fargate service             | Same image. Worker:Enabled is true. Scales on queue depth.                                                                                                                                        |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| One-off tasks    | ECS task definition             | Same image. Started by the pipeline or a developer with a command: migrate or import-catalog.                                                                                                     |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Database         | Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 | pgvector enabled. Automated backups. Credentials in Secrets Manager.                                                                                                                              |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Files            | S3 buckets                      | Documents: private, versioned, encrypted with a KMS key; CORS allows uploads from the frontend origin. Catalog: private, read only by the one-off task. Frontend: served only through CloudFront. |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Queues           | SQS                             | document-queue and assessment-queue, each with a dead-letter queue and a limit of three receives                                                                                                  |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Models           | Bedrock                         | Access enabled for the Claude model and the Titan embedding model                                                                                                                                 |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Text recognition | Textract                        | Asynchronous text detection on S3 objects                                                                                                                                                         |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Sign-in          | Cognito user pool               | Multi-factor required. Self-registration off.                                                                                                                                                     |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Edge             | CloudFront                      | Serves the frontend and forwards /api/\* to the load balancer, so both share one origin                                                                                                           |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Images           | ECR                             | One repository for the application image                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---              | ---                             | ---                                                                                                                                                                                               |

**Permissions**

- The API and worker run under task roles. There are no access keys (QR-3).
- The API role can issue links for the documents bucket, send to the queues, and manage Cognito users.
- The worker role can read and write the documents bucket, read and send to the queues, and call Bedrock and Textract.
- The one-off task role can read the catalog bucket and the database secret.

**Environments**

There are two environments, development and production, in separate AWS accounts. Production holds client documents, and development never does.

**Deployment**

1. The pipeline builds and tests the application, then pushes the image to ECR.
2. It runs the database migrations as a one-off ECS task, with the migrate command.
3. It runs cdk deploy, which rolls the API and worker services to the new image. New tasks must pass their health check before old ones stop.

Migrations must work with both the old and the new image, because the old one keeps running until step 3 finishes.

The catalog import is not part of a release. A developer puts a new catalog file in the catalog bucket and runs the one-off task with import-catalog. It runs in one transaction and never deletes a control.

## Operations

**Logging**

- Logs are structured JSON, sent to CloudWatch.
- Each request gets a correlation ID. The ID travels in every queue message, so the logs of a request and the work it started can be read together (QR-8).
- Logs never contain document text, quotes or prompts.

**Alarms**

| Alarm                                           | Meaning                                         |
| ----------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- |
| A dead-letter queue is not empty                | A document or control failed three times (QR-6) |
| ---                                             | ---                                             |
| The oldest queue message is over 30 minutes old | The worker is stuck or too small                |
| ---                                             | ---                                             |
| API 5xx rate is above 1%                        | The API is failing                              |
| ---                                             | ---                                             |
| Database capacity is at its maximum             | The capacity limit needs raising                |
| ---                                             | ---                                             |

**Health**

The API exposes /health, which checks the database connection. The load balancer uses it.

**Testing**

| Kind        | Covers                                                                                    | Tools                      |
| ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------- |
| Unit        | Citation checking, verdict rules, chunking, access check (404 before 403), decision rules | xUnit                      |
| ---         | ---                                                                                       | ---                        |
| Integration | Endpoints, pipeline steps and search against real PostgreSQL, S3 and SQS                  | Testcontainers, LocalStack |
| ---         | ---                                                                                       | ---                        |
| Isolation   | A search in one engagement returns nothing from another (QR-1)                            | Integration suite          |
| ---         | ---                                                                                       | ---                        |
| Search plan | Vector search uses the partial HNSW index                                                 | Integration suite          |
| ---         | ---                                                                                       | ---                        |
| Concurrency | Close against run start, delete during processing, decision against a re-run              | Integration suite          |
| ---         | ---                                                                                       | ---                        |

Bedrock and Textract are replaced by fakes in unit and integration tests.
